facts.statement: Taohelong possessed a sacral shield, which is a carpet of osteoderms covering the hips similar to those found in other ankylosaurians.
facts.quote: The animal's armor includes part of a "sacral shield", a carpet of osteoderms over the hips found in some other ankylosaurians.

facts.statement: The neural channel of Taohelong's tail vertebra has a cross-section shaped like an inverted trapezium.
facts.quote: The neural channel of the tail vertebra has a cross-section like an inverted trapezium.

facts.statement: The outer rim of Taohelong's ilium has a profile resembling a mirrored 'S' when viewed from the top.
facts.quote: In top view the profile of the outer rim of the ilium is like a mirrored "S".

facts.statement: The osteoderms making up Taohelong's sacral shield are irregular in both their shape and size.
facts.quote: The osteoderms of the sacral shield are irregular in both shape and size.

facts.statement: The only known fossil of Taohelong was discovered in the Lanzhou-Minhe Basin near the border of Yongjing and Lintao counties by the Gansu Zhendan Dinosaur Culture Communication Company.
facts.quote: The only known fossil of Taohelong was found in the Lanzhou-Minhe Basin near the border of Yongjing and Lintao counties by the Gansu Zhendan Dinosaur Culture Communication Company.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen GSDM 00021 was described in 2013 by Yang Jingtao, You Hailu, Li Daqing, and Kong Delai as the new ankylosaur taxon Taohelong jinchengensis.
facts.quote: GSDM 00021 was described in 2013 by paleontologists Yang Jingtao, You Hailu, Li Daqing, and Kong Delai where it was designated the holotype of the new taxon of ankylosaur Taohelong jinchengensis.

facts.statement: The genus name Taohelong refers to the Tao River, while the species name jinchengensis references the ancient name of Lanzhou, Jincheng, meaning 'solid' to describe the animal's armor.
facts.quote: The genus name is taken from the Tao River that flows through the fossil deposits, while the species name is after the ancient name of Lanzhou, Jincheng, which also translates as "solid" in reference to the armor over the back of the animal.

facts.statement: A sauropod distinct from Huanghetitan and Daxiatitan was found 200 meters away from the Taohelong fossil site within the Hekou Group.
facts.quote: A sauropod, distinct from Huanghetitan and Daxiatitan that are known from elsewhere in the Hekou Group of Lanzhoue-Minhe Basin, was found 200 m away.

facts.statement: Taohelong is classified within the family Nodosauridae, specifically in the subfamily Polacanthinae.
facts.quote: Taohelong was placed in the Nodosauridae, more precisely in the Polacanthinae.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis identifies Taohelong as the sister taxon to Polacanthus foxii, making it the first described polacanthine from Asia.
facts.quote: Yang et al. performed a phylogenetic analysis and found Taohelong to be the sister taxon to Polacanthus foxii, making it the first polacanthine to be described from Asia.

facts.statement: Taohelong jinchengensis lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 113 to 110 million years ago in the Aptian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Taohelong jinchengensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Taohelong de dinosaurio tireóforo nodosáurido que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 113 a 110 millones de años, durante el Aptiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Taohelon lived from the Barremian to the Aptian, spanning from 125.77 to 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Taohelong was named and described in 2013 by Yang Jing-Tao, You Hai-Lu, Li Da-Qing, and Kong De-Lai.
facts.quote: Taohelong was named and described in 2013 by Yang Jing-Tao, You Hai-Lu, Li Da-Qing, and Kong De-Lai.

rejected.statement: Taohelong fossils were found in the Lower Cretaceous Hekou Group, which can be informally divided into eight subunits in the region.
rejected.quote: The deposits Taohelong was found within pertain to the Lower Cretaceous Hekou Group, which can be informally divided into eight subunits in the region.
